name: Titanium.UI.WebView
summary: The web view allows you to open an HTML5 based view which can load either local or remote content.
description:
Use the [Titanium.UI.createWebView](api:Titanium.UI#createWebView) method or **``** Alloy element to create a web view. Web views are more expensive to create than other native views because of the requirement to load the HTML browser into memory. The web view content can be any valid web content such as HTML, PDF, SVG or other WebKit supported content types. #### JavaScript Context in WebViews--Local vs. Remote Content JavaScript in the web view executes in its own context. The web view can interact with this content, but most of this functionality is limited to local content. **Local Scripts** When running local web content (that is, content that is included in the application's resources), scripts have access to the Titanium namespace. In particular, when running local web content: - You can use [Titanium.App.addEventListener](api:Titanium.App#addEventListener) and [Titanium.App.fireEvent](api:Titanium.App#fireEvent) to receive and send application-level events. - Events can be logged using the [Titanium.API](api:Titanium.API) logging methods. **Remote Scripts** Scripts downloaded from remote web servers cannot access the Titanium namespace. To interact with remote content, wait until the content is loaded, then use the [evalJS](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#evalJS) method to execute a JavaScript expression inside the web view and retrieve the value of an expression. To trigger a message from the remote web page, refer to [Titanium.UI.WebView.addScriptMessageHandler](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#addScriptMessageHandler). You can inject the local `Ti.App.fireEvent` bindings yourself by adding a script element using evalJS. ```js webview.evalJS( 'javascript=(function addBinding(){' + 'var s=document.createElement("script");' + 's.setAttribute("type","text/javascript");' + 's.innerHTML="' + /* insert content of binding.min.js */ + '";' + 'document.getElementsByTagName("body")[0].appendChild(s);' + '})()' ); ``` The `binding.min.js` is available in the [repository](https://github.com/tidev/titanium-sdk/tree/main/android/modules/ui/assets/Resources/ti.internal/webview). #### Local JavaScript Files During the build process for creating a package, all JavaScript files, that is, any file with a '.js' extension, are removed and their content is encrypted and obfuscated into one resource, causing these files to not load properly in a WebView if they are loaded externally. For JavaScript files referenced in static local HTML files, these JavaScript files are omitted from processing and left intact, which means they can be correctly loaded in the WebView. For local JavaScript files not referenced in static local HTML files, for example, a dynamically-generated HTML file referencing a local JavaScript file, rename the file extension of the local JavaScript files to '.jslocal' instead of '.js'. The build process for testing your application on the simulator, emulator or device does not affect the loading of local JavaScript files. #### iOS Platform Implementation Notes On the iOS platform, the native web view handles scrolling and other related touch events internally. If you add event listeners on the web view **or its parent views** for any of the standard touch events (`touchstart`, `click`, and so on), these events do not reach the native web view, and the user will not be able to scroll, zoom, click on links, and so on. To prevent this default behavior, set [willHandleTouches](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#willHandleTouches) to `false`. In other words, you can have either Titanium-style events against the web view instance, or internal JavaScript events in the DOM, but not both. #### Android Platform Implementation Notes **Android 4.4 and Later Support** Starting with Android 4.4 (API Level 19), the WebView component is based off of Chromium, introducing a number of changes to its rendering engine. Web content may look or behave differently depending on the Android version. The WebView does not have full feature parity with Chrome for Android. By default, the Chromium WebView uses hardware acceleration, which may cause content to fail to render. If the WebView fails to render the content, the web view will clear itself, displaying only the default background color. The following log messages will be displayed in the console: ``` [WARN] : AwContents: nativeOnDraw failed; clearing to background color. [INFO] : chromium: [INFO:async_pixel_transfer_manager_android.cc(56)] ``` To workaround this issue, you can enable software rendering by setting the WebView's [borderRadius](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#borderRadius) property to a value greater than zero. If you are developing local HTML content and size your elements using percentages, the WebView may not calculate the sizes correctly when hardware acceleration is enabled, resulting in the same behavior previously mentioned. To workaround this issue, you can use the previously mentioned workaround to enable software rendering, use absolute size values or use the [onresize](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window.onresize) event to set the heights of the components. For example, if you have a div element with an id set to `component` that needs to use the entire web view, the following callback resizes the content to use the full height of the web view: ``` js window.onresize= function(){ document.getElementById("component").style.height = window.innerHeight + 'px'; }; ``` For more information, see the following topics: * [Android Developers: Migrating to WebView in Android 4.4](https://developer.android.com/guide/webapps/migrating.html) * [Google Chrome: WebView for Android](https://developer.chrome.com/multidevice/webview/overview) **Plugin Support** The Android web view supports native plugins. To use plugin content, you must set the [pluginState](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#pluginState) property to either [WEBVIEW_PLUGINS_ON](api:Titanium.UI.Android#WEBVIEW_PLUGINS_ON) or [WEBVIEW_PLUGINS_ON_DEMAND](api:Titanium.UI.Android#WEBVIEW_PLUGINS_ON_DEMAND). You must also call [pause](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#pause) when the current activity is paused, to prevent plugin content from continuing to run in the background. Call [resume](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#resume) when the current activity is resumed. You can do this by adding listeners for the [Activity.pause](Titanium.Android.Activity.pause) and [Activity.resume](Titanium.Android.Activity.resume) events. **Accessing Cookies** On Android, the web view uses the system cookie store which does not share cookies with the [Titanium.Network.HTTPClient](api:Titanium.Network.HTTPClient) cookie store. Developers can manage their cookies for both cookie stores using the methods [Titanium.Network.addHTTPCookie](api:Titanium.Network#addHTTPCookie), [Titanium.Network.addSystemCookie](api:Titanium.Network#addSystemCookie), [Titanium.Network.getHTTPCookies](api:Titanium.Network#getHTTPCookies), [Titanium.Network.getHTTPCookiesForDomain](api:Titanium.Network#getHTTPCookiesForDomain), [Titanium.Network.getSystemCookies](api:Titanium.Network#getSystemCookies), [Titanium.Network.removeHTTPCookie](api:Titanium.Network#removeHTTPCookie), [Titanium.Network.removeHTTPCookiesForDomain](api:Titanium.Network#removeHTTPCookiesForDomain), [Titanium.Network.removeAllHTTPCookies](api:Titanium.Network#removeAllHTTPCookies), [Titanium.Network.removeSystemCookie](api:Titanium.Network#removeSystemCookie), [Titanium.Network.removeAllSystemCookies](api:Titanium.Network#removeAllSystemCookies). **WKWebView** With Titanium SDK 8.0.0, we now use WKWebView to implement Ti.UI.WebView (as Apple has deprecated UIWebView). WKWebView has few restriction specially with local file accessing. For supporting custom-fonts with WKWebView a little modification is required in the HTML files: ``` html ``` To have a WKWebView scale the page the same way as UIWebView, add the following meta tag to the HTML header: ``` html ``` ### Ti.UI.SIZE and WebViews With Titanium 8.0.0+, [Titanium.UI.SIZE](api:Titanium.UI#SIZE) does not work for WebViews. We recommend to give a **fixed height** to [Titanium.UI.WebView](api:Titanium.UI.WebView) (as noted in [TIDOC-3355](https://jira-archive.titaniumsdk.com/TIDOC-3355)). As a workaround you can try to get the `document.body.scrollHeight` inside [Titanium.UI.WebView.load](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#load) event of webview and set the height to webview. See following example. ``` js var win = Ti.UI.createWindow(); var verticalView = Ti.UI.createView({layout: 'vertical', width: "100%", height: "100%"}); verticalView.add(Ti.UI.createLabel({text: 'Label 1', top: 30, width: Ti.UI.SIZE, height: Ti.UI.SIZE})); var htmla = "
  • Item 1
  • Item 2
"; var html = ""; html += ""; html += htmla; html += ""; var webview = Ti.UI.createWebView({left: '14dp', right: '14dp', top: '7dp', height: Ti.UI.SIZE, html: html, backgroundColor: "yellow"}); verticalView.add(webview); verticalView.add(Ti.UI.createLabel({text: 'Label 2', top: 30, width: Ti.UI.SIZE, height: Ti.UI.SIZE})); win.add(verticalView); win.open(); webview.addEventListener('load', function(e) { var result = webview.evalJSSync('document.body.scrollHeight'); Ti.API.info('webview height: ' + result); webview.height = result; }); ``` #### For More Information See [Integrating Web Content](https://titaniumsdk.com/guide/Titanium_SDK/Titanium_SDK_How-tos/Integrating_Web_Content/) in the Titanium Mobile Guides for more information on using web views, including use cases, more code examples, and best practices for web view content.

examples.title: Basic Web View to External URL
Alloy XML Markup
examples.code:
Previous example as an Alloy view.

``` xml
<Alloy>
    <Window id="win" modal="true">
        <WebView id="webview" url="http://www.titaniumsdk.com" />
    </Window>
</Alloy>
```

examples.title: Listening to Web View properties in iOS
Usage of allowedURLSchemes and handleurl in iOS

properties.name: allowedURLSchemes
properties.summary: List of allowed URL schemes for the web view.
properties.description: See the example section "Usage of allowedURLSchemes and handleurl in iOS".

properties.name: allowFileAccess
properties.summary: A Boolean value indicating file access within WebView.
properties.description: Set to `true` to enable access to local files for examples images stored in [Titanium.Filesystem.applicationDataDirectory](api:Titanium.Filesystem#applicationDataDirectory). If false resources are still accessible using `file:///android_asset` and `file:///android_res`. Do not enable this if your app accepts arbitrary URLs from external sources.

properties.name: allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures
properties.summary: A Boolean value indicating whether horizontal swipe gestures will trigger back-forward list navigation.

properties.name: allowsLinkPreview
properties.summary:
A Boolean value that determines whether pressing on a link displays a preview of the
destination for the link.
properties.description:
This property is available on devices that support 3D Touch. Default value is `false`.

If you set this value to `true` for a web view, users (with devices that support 3D Touch)
can preview link destinations, and can preview detected data such as addresses, by pressing on links.
Such previews are known to users as peeks. If a user presses deeper, the preview navigates (or pops,
in user terminology) to the destination. Because pop navigation switches the user from your app to
Safari, it is opt-in, by way of this property, rather default behavior for this class.

properties.name: assetsDirectory
properties.summary: Path of file or directory to allow read access by the WebView.
properties.description:
Use this property to change the resources the web view has access to when loading the content of a local file.
By default the web view only has access to files inside the same directory as the loaded file. To reference
resources from other directories (e.g. a parent directory) change this property accordingly.

If assetsDirectory references a single file, only that file may be loaded. If assetsDirectory references a
directory, files inside that directory may be loaded.

This property needs to be set before [url](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#url) is assigned to a local file.

properties.name: autoAdjustScrollViewInsets
properties.summary: Specifies whether or not the web view should automatically adjust its scroll view insets.
properties.description:
When the value is `true`, it allows the web view to adjust its scroll view insets in response
to the screen areas consumed by the status bar, navigation bar, toolbar and tab bar (safe areas).

This is useful when displaying a web view that extends under navigation bars or into
safe area regions, ensuring content is not obscured.

The default behavior assumes that this is `false`.

properties.name: blacklistedURLs
properties.summary: An array of URL strings to blacklist.
properties.description:
An array of URL strings to blacklist. This will stop the webview from going to URLs listed in
the blacklist. Note, this only applies in the links clicked inside the webview. The first website
that is loaded will not be stopped even if it matches the blacklist.

properties.name: blockedURLs
properties.summary: An array of URL strings to be blocked.
properties.description:
An array of URL strings to be blocked from loading. This will stop the webview from going to URLs
listed in this array. Note that this only applies to the links tapped on by the end-user.
The first website that is loaded will not be stopped, even if it is listed in the blocklist.

properties.name: cacheMode
properties.summary: Determines how a cache is used in this web view.

properties.name: cachePolicy
properties.summary: The cache policy for the request.

properties.name: configuration
properties.summary: The configuration for the new web view.
properties.description: This property can only be set when creating the webview and will be ignored when set afterwards.

properties.name: data
properties.summary: Web content to load.
properties.description:
Android only supports loading data from a `Blob`, not a `File`.

See also: [url](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#url) and [html](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#html).

properties.name: disableBounce
properties.summary: Determines whether the view will bounce when scrolling to the edge of the scrollable region.
properties.description: Set to `true` to disable the bounce effect.

properties.name: disableContextMenu
properties.summary: Determines whether or not the webview should not be able to display the context menu.
properties.description:
Set to `true` to disable the context menu. Note that disabling the context menu will
also disable the text selection on iOS.

properties.name: enableJavascriptInterface
properties.summary: Enable adding JavaScript interfaces internally to webview prior to JELLY_BEAN_MR1 (Android 4.2)
properties.description: This property is introduced to prevent a security issue with older devices (< JELLY_BEAN_MR1)

properties.name: enableZoomControls
properties.summary: If `true`, zoom controls are enabled.

properties.name: handlePlatformUrl
properties.summary: Lets the webview handle platform supported urls
properties.description:
By default any urls that are not handled by the Titanium platform but can be handled by the
shared application are automatically sent to the shared application and the webview does not
open these. When this property is set to `true` the webview will attempt to handle these
urls and they will not be sent to the shared application. An example is links to telephone
numbers.

deprecated.notes:
This property in no more supported in Titanium SDK 8.0.0+. Use property <Titanium.UI.WebView.allowedURLSchemes>
in conjunction with <Titanium.UI.WebView.handleurl>. See the example section
"Usage of allowedURLSchemes and handleurl in iOS".

properties.name: hideKeyboardAccessoryView
properties.summary: A Boolean value indicating whether to hide the keyboard accessory bar.
properties.description:
When this property is set to `true`, the keyboard accessory bar (the bar with "Previous",
"Next" and "Done" buttons that appears above the keyboard when focusing input fields in
web content) is hidden. This can be useful when you want to provide your own custom
input accessory or simply want a cleaner keyboard appearance.

Set to `false` (the default) to show the standard keyboard accessory bar.

properties.name: hideLoadIndicator
properties.summary: Hides activity indicator when loading remote URL.

properties.name: html
properties.summary: HTML content of this web view.

properties.name: ignoreSslError
properties.summary: Controls whether to ignore invalid SSL certificates or not.
properties.description:
If set to `true`, the web page loads despite having an invalid SSL certificate.
If set to `false`, a web page with an invalid SSL certificate does not load.

iOS Note: As soon as you set this property to `true`, iOS will cache the response
for the lifetime of the current web view.

properties.name: keyboardDisplayRequiresUserAction
properties.summary: A Boolean value indicating whether web content can programmatically display the keyboard.
properties.description:
When this property is set to true, the user must explicitly tap the elements in the web view
to display the keyboard (or other relevant input view) for that element. When set to false,
a focus event on an element causes the input view to be displayed and associated with
that element automatically.

properties.name: LAYER_TYPE_HARDWARE
properties.summary: Hardware rendering mode

properties.name: LAYER_TYPE_NONE
properties.summary: Default rendering mode

properties.name: LAYER_TYPE_SOFTWARE
properties.summary: Software rendering mode

properties.name: layerType
properties.summary: A value indicating the render mode of the WebView
properties.description:
Set to Ti.UI.WebView.LAYER_TYPE_SOFTWARE (software rendering) if you use `Ti.Media.takeScreenshot()` or `toImage()` and the WebView contains local HTML files.
Otherwise the WebView might be empty in the screenshot/image. If you change the setting you will have to assign the HTML content again.

properties.name: lightTouchEnabled
properties.summary: Enables using light touches to make a selection and activate mouseovers.
properties.description:
Setting this property solves the problem of web links with specific length not triggering a link click in Android.

This is only an Android specific property and has no effect starting from API level 18.

This flag is `true` by default to retain backwards compatibility with previous
behavior.

properties.name: loading
properties.summary: Indicates if the webview is loading content.

properties.name: mixedContentMode
properties.summary: If `true`, allows the loading of insecure resources from a secure origin.
properties.description:
On iOS this functionality can be set in the `<plist>` section of the tiapp.xml
using the `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` key as part of the App Transport Security.
The plist key is enabled by default, allowing arbitrary loads to be processed.

properties.name: multipleWindows
properties.summary: If set to `false` it will prevent the WebView from opening new windows/tabs.

properties.name: onCreateWindow
properties.summary:
Callback function called when there is a request for the application to create a new window
to host new content.

properties.name: onlink
properties.summary: Fired before navigating to a link.
properties.description:
The callback will be called before navigating to the link. The Boolean return value of the
callback will determine if the link will be navigated or discarded.

inlined.name: OnLinkURLResponse
inlined.summary: An object returned when the [Titanium.UI.WebView.onlink](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#onlink) callback is fired.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: The URL of the link that should be navigated to.

properties.name: overScrollMode
properties.summary: Determines the behavior when the user overscrolls the view.

properties.name: PDF_PAGE_DIN_A1
properties.summary: PDF paper size

properties.name: PDF_PAGE_DIN_A2
properties.summary: PDF paper size

properties.name: PDF_PAGE_DIN_A3
properties.summary: PDF paper size

properties.name: PDF_PAGE_DIN_A4
properties.summary: PDF paper size

properties.name: PDF_PAGE_DIN_A5
properties.summary: PDF paper size

properties.name: pluginState
properties.summary: Determines how to treat content that requires plugins in this web view.
properties.description:
This setting affects the loading of content that requires web plugins.

To enable hardware acceleration, add the `tool-api-level` and
`manifest` elements shown below inside the `android` element in your `tiapp.xml` file.

``` xml
<android xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">
    <tool-api-level>11</tool-api-level>
    <manifest>
        <application android:hardwareAccelerated="true"/>
    </manifest>
</android>
```

See Android documentation for
[WebSettings.PluginState](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/webkit/WebSettings.PluginState.html).

This property only works on Android devices at API Level 8 or greater.

properties.name: progress
properties.summary: An estimate of what fraction of the current navigation has been loaded.
properties.description:
This value ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 based on the total number of bytes expected
to be received, including the main document and all of its potential subresources.
After loading completes, the progress remains at 1.0 until a new download starts,
at which point progress is reset to 0.0.

properties.name: requestHeaders
properties.summary: Sets extra request headers for this web view to use on subsequent URL requests.
properties.description:
Setting this property allows you to set custom headers to the URL requests.
The parameter will be key-value pairs: `{"Custom-field1":"value1", "Custom-field2":"value2"}`

On Android you should avoid Calling `setRequestHeaders()` right after `createWebView()`. Use the `requestHeaders` property
inside `createWebView()` or put it inside the window `open` event.

properties.name: scalesPageToFit
properties.summary: If `true`, scale contents to fit the web view.
properties.description:
On iOS, setting this to `true` sets the initial zoom level to show the entire
page, and enables the user to zoom the web view in and out. Setting this to
`false` prevents the user from zooming the web view.

On Android, only controls the initial zoom level.
properties.default:
`false` on iOS. On Android, `false` when content is specified as a local URL,
`true` for any other kind of content (remote URL, `Blob`, or `File`).

properties.name: scrollbars
properties.summary: Enable or disable horizontal/vertical scrollbars in a WebView.

properties.name: scrollsToTop
properties.summary: Controls whether the scroll-to-top gesture is effective.
properties.description:
The scroll-to-top gesture is a tap on the status bar; The default value of this property is true.
This gesture works when you have a single visible web view.
If there are multiple table views, web views, text areas, and/or scroll views visible,
you will need to disable (set to false) on the above views you DON'T want this
behaviour on. The remaining view will then respond to scroll-to-top gesture.

properties.name: secure
properties.summary:
A Boolean value indicating whether all resources on the page have been loaded through
securely encrypted connections.

properties.name: selectionGranularity
properties.summary: The level of granularity with which the user can interactively select content in the web view.

properties.name: timeout
properties.summary: The timeout interval for the request, in seconds.

properties.name: title
properties.summary: Returns page title of webpage.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: URL to the web document.
properties.description:
This property changes as the content of the webview changes (such as when the user
clicks a hyperlink inside the web view).

See also: [data](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#data) and [html](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#html).

properties.name: userAgent
properties.summary: The User-Agent header used by the web view when requesting content.
properties.description:
On the iOS platform, this is not per-webview. Once you have set this property for a webview
it will not change for same. But while creating new webview it can be changed to new user agent.

On Android, changing the user agent after the webview has begun loading content may cause
the webview to reload and fire multiple `load` or `beforeload` events. Developers should provide the
user agent value in the creation properties to avoid the reload and multiple events firing.

properties.name: willHandleTouches
properties.summary: Explicitly specifies if this web view handles touches.
properties.description:
On the iOS platform, if this web view **or any of its parent views** have touch
listeners, the Titanium component intercepts **all** touch events. This
prevents the user from interacting with the native web view components.

Set this flag to `false` to disable the default behavior. Setting this property to `false`
allows the user to interact with the native web view and still honor any `touch` events sent to
its parents. No `touch` events will be generated when the user interacts with the web view itself.

Set this flag to `true` if you want to receive touch events from the web view and
the user does not need to interact with the web content directly.

This flag is `true` by default to retain backwards compatibility with previous
behavior.

properties.name: zoomLevel
properties.summary: Manage the zoom-level of the current page.
properties.default: undefined. Behaves as no zoom applied.

methods.summary: Adds a script message handler.

parameters.summary: The name of the message handler, other than the reserved '_Ti_', or '_Ti_Cookie_'.

methods.name: addUserScript
methods.summary: Adds a user script.

parameters.name: params
parameters.summary: Properties required to create user script.

inlined.name: UserScriptParams
inlined.summary: Dictionary of options for the [Titanium.UI.WebView.addUserScript](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#addUserScript) method.

properties.name: injectionTime
properties.summary: The time when the script should be injected into the webpage.

properties.name: mainFrameOnly
properties.summary:
A Boolean value indicating whether the script should be injected only into the
main frame (true) or into all frames (false).

properties.name: source
properties.summary: A script that can be injected into a webpage.

methods.name: backForwardList
methods.summary: An object which maintains a list of visited pages used to go back and forward to the most recent page.

methods.name: canGoBack
methods.summary: Returns `true` if the web view can go back in its history list.

methods.name: canGoForward
methods.summary: Returns `true` if the web view can go forward in its history list.

methods.name: createPDF
methods.summary: Create a PDF document representation from the web page currently displayed in the WebView.

parameters.name: pageWidth
parameters.summary: The width in mils (thousandths of an inch) of the PDF (Android only)

parameters.name: pageHeight
parameters.summary: The height in mils (thousandths of an inch) of the PDF (Android only)

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.summary: Predefined size. (Android only)

parameters.name: showMenu
parameters.summary: Will show Androids printing menu. No success callback afterwards. (Android only)

parameters.name: firstPageOnly
parameters.summary: Only print first page (Android only)

parameters.name: success
parameters.summary: Function to call upon PDF creation. (Android only)

properties.summary: The created data.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.summary: Function to call upon PDF creation. (iOS only)

inlined.name: DataCreationResult
inlined.summary: The parameter passed to the [Titanium.UI.WebView.createPDF](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#createPDF) or [Titanium.UI.WebView.createWebArchive](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#createWebArchive)callback.

properties.name: data
properties.summary: The created data.

properties.name: error
properties.summary: Error message, if any returned.
properties.description: May be undefined.

properties.name: success
properties.summary: Indicates if the data creation successful or not.
properties.description: Returns `true` on successful creation, otherwise `false`.

methods.name: createWebArchive
methods.summary: Create WebKit web archive data representing the current web content of the WebView.
methods.description:
WebKit web archive data represents a snapshot of web content. It can be loaded into a WebView directly,
and saved to a file for later use.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.summary: Function to call upon web archive creation.

inlined.name: DataCreationResult
inlined.summary: The parameter passed to the [Titanium.UI.WebView.createPDF](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#createPDF) or [Titanium.UI.WebView.createWebArchive](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#createWebArchive)callback.

properties.name: data
properties.summary: The created data.

properties.name: error
properties.summary: Error message, if any returned.
properties.description: May be undefined.

properties.name: success
properties.summary: Indicates if the data creation successful or not.
properties.description: Returns `true` on successful creation, otherwise `false`.

methods.name: evalJS
methods.summary:
Evaluates a JavaScript expression inside the context of the web view and
optionally, returns a result. If a callback function is passed in as second argument,
the evaluation will take place asynchronously and the the callback function will be called with the result.

parameters.name: code
parameters.summary: JavaScript code as a string. The code will be evaluated inside the web view context.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.summary: Optional callback function for the result. Required on Windows, optional on iOS/Android.

returns.summary: Result of the evaluation. May be null if the asynchronous variant of this method is called.

methods.name: findString
methods.summary: Searches the page contents for the given string.

parameters.name: searchString
parameters.summary: The string to search for.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary: Options for search.

inlined.name: StringSearchOptions
inlined.summary:
The optional options to pass to the [Titanium.UI.WebView.findString](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#findString). Pass a
dictionary with one or more of the following string-keys:
    * `caseSensitive` (Boolean value)
    * `backward` (Boolean value)
    * `wraps` (Boolean value)

properties.name: backward
properties.summary: The direction to search from the current selection. The search will respect the writing direction of the document

properties.name: caseSensitive
properties.summary: Whether or not the search should be case sensitive.

properties.name: wraps
properties.summary: Whether the search should start at the beginning of the document once it reaches the end.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.summary: Function to call upon search finished.

properties.name: error
properties.summary: Error message, if any returned.
properties.description: May be undefined.

properties.name: success
properties.summary: Indicates if string found or not.
properties.description: Returns `true` if found, otherwise `false`.

methods.name: goBack
methods.summary: Goes back one entry in the web view's history list, to the previous page.

methods.name: goForward
methods.summary: Goes forward one entry in this web view's history list, if possible.

methods.name: pause
methods.summary: Pauses native webview plugins.
methods.description:
Add a `pause` handler to your [Titanium.Android.Activity](api:Titanium.Android.Activity) and invoke
this method to pause native plugins.

Call [resume](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#resume) to unpause native plugins.

methods.name: release
methods.summary: Releases memory when the web view is no longer needed.

methods.name: reload
methods.summary: Reloads the current webpage.

methods.name: removeAllUserScripts
methods.summary: Removes all associated user scripts.

methods.name: removeScriptMessageHandler
methods.summary: Removes a script message handler.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The name of the message handler.

methods.name: repaint
methods.summary: Forces the web view to repaint its contents.

methods.name: resume
methods.summary: Resume native webview plugins.
methods.description:
Used to unpause native plugins after calling [pause](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#pause).

Add a `resume` handler to your [Titanium.Android.Activity](api:Titanium.Android.Activity) and invoke
this method to resume native plugins.

methods.name: setBasicAuthentication
methods.summary: Sets the basic authentication for this web view to use on subsequent URL requests.
methods.description:
The persistence property of this method is only supported on iOS and Titanium SDK 8.0.0+.
It is ignored on other platforms and versions.

parameters.name: username
parameters.summary: Basic auth user name.

parameters.name: password
parameters.summary: Basic auth password.

parameters.name: persistence
parameters.summary:
Constants specify how long the credential will be kept.
This is only supported on iOS and Titanium SDK 8.0.0+.

methods.name: setHtml
methods.summary: Sets the value of [html](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#html) property.
methods.description: The `options` parameter can be used to specify two options that affect the WebView main content presentation: * `baseURL`. Sets the URL that the web content's paths will be relative to. * `mimeType`. Sets the MIME type for the content. Defaults to "text/html" if not specified. For example: ``` js setHtml('Hello, Titanium!', { baseURL: 'https://titaniumsdk.com/' }); ```

parameters.name: html
parameters.summary: New HTML to display in the web view.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary: Optional parameters for the content. Only used by iOS and Android.

properties.name: baseURL
properties.summary: Sets the URL that the web content's paths will be relative to.

properties.name: mimeType
properties.summary: Sets the MIME type for the content. Defaults to "text/html" if not specified.

methods.name: startListeningToProperties
methods.summary: Add native properties for observing for change.
methods.description:
Some common properties are title, URL, estimatedProgress etc.
See native KVO capability at https://developer.apple.com/documentation/webkit/wkwebview.
See example section "Listening to Web View properties in iOS" for usage.

parameters.name: propertyList
parameters.summary: List of properties for listen.

methods.name: stopListeningToProperties
methods.summary: Remove native properties from observing.

parameters.name: propertyList
parameters.summary: List of properties to remove.

methods.name: stopLoading
methods.summary: Stops loading a currently loading page.

methods.name: takeSnapshot
methods.summary: Takes a snapshot of the view's visible viewport.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.summary: Function to call upon snapshot captured.

inlined.name: SnapshotResult
inlined.summary: The parameter passed to the [Titanium.UI.WebView.takeSnapshot](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#takeSnapshot) callback.

properties.name: error
properties.summary: Error message, if any returned.
properties.description: May be undefined.

properties.name: snapshot
properties.summary: The snapshot image.

properties.name: success
properties.summary: Indicates if the snapshot taken.
properties.description: Returns `true` on successful snapshot captured, otherwise `false`.

events.name: beforeload
events.summary: Fired before the web view starts loading its content.
events.description:
This event may fire multiple times depending on the content or URL.  For example, if you set
the URL of the web view to a URL that redirects to another URL, such as an HTTP URL
redirecting to an HTTPS URL, this event is fired for the original URL and the redirect URL.

This event does not fire when navigating remote web pages.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: URL of the web document being loaded.

properties.name: navigationType
properties.summary: Constant indicating the user's action.

properties.name: isMainFrame
properties.summary: Indicate if the event was generated from the main page or an iframe.

events.name: blacklisturl
events.summary: Fired when a blacklisted URL is stopped.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: The URL of the web document that is stopped.

events.name: blockedurl
events.summary: Fired when a URL has been blocked from loading.
events.description:
This event is fired when the end-user attempts to navigate to a website matching a URL in
the [Titanium.UI.WebView.blockedURLs](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#blockedURLs) property.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: The URL of the web document that has been blocked from loading.

events.name: error
events.summary: Fired when the web view cannot load the content.
events.description:
The `errorCode` value refers to one of the [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI) URL_ERROR constants or, if it does not
match one of those constants, it refers to a platform-specific constant. The platform-specific
values are underlying [iOS NSURLError*](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/1508628-url_loading_system_error_codes)
or [Android WebViewClient ERROR_*](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/webkit/WebViewClient.html) constants.

properties.name: success
properties.summary: Indicates a successful operation. Returns `false`.

properties.name: error
properties.summary: Error message, if any returned. May be undefined.

properties.name: code
properties.summary:
Error code.
If the error was generated by the operating system, that system's error value
is used. Otherwise, this value will be -1.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: URL of the web document.

events.name: handleurl
events.summary: Fired when [Titanium.UI.WebView.allowedURLSchemes](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#allowedURLSchemes) contains scheme of opening url.
events.description: See the example section "Usage of allowedURLSchemes and handleurl in iOS".

properties.name: handler
properties.summary: Handler [Titanium.UI.iOS.WebViewDecisionHandler](api:Titanium.UI.iOS.WebViewDecisionHandler).

properties.name: url
properties.summary: URL of the web document being loaded.

events.name: load
events.summary: Fired when the web view content is loaded.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: URL of the web document.

events.name: message
events.summary: Fired when a script message is received from a webpage.
events.description:
This event get fired when you have added a message handler using [Titanium.UI.WebView.addScriptMessageHandler](api:Titanium.UI.WebView#addScriptMessageHandler)
and the webpage sends a message to it.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: URL of the web document being loaded.

properties.name: body
properties.summary: The body of the message sent from webview.

properties.name: name
properties.summary: The name of the message handler to which the message is sent.

properties.name: isMainFrame
properties.summary: A Boolean value indicating whether the frame is the web site's main frame or a subframe.

events.name: onLoadResource
events.description: Android only. Notify the host application that the WebView will load the resource specified by the given URL.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: The URL of the resource that will load.

events.name: progress
events.description:
Provides a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0, where 0.0 indicates nothing was downloaded and
1.0 means the page and all of its resources has finished downloading.

properties.name: value
properties.summary: An estimate of what fraction of the current navigation has been loaded.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: URL of the web document being loaded.

events.name: redirect
events.summary: Fired when a web view receives a server redirect.

properties.name: title
properties.summary: Page title of webpage.

properties.name: url
properties.summary: URL of the web document being loaded.

events.name: sslerror
events.summary: Fired when an SSL error occurred.
events.description:
This is a synchronous event and the developer can change the value of `ignoreSslError`
to control if the request should proceed or fail.

properties.name: code
properties.summary: SSL error code.
